access_notes: The museum's record (asset 25064) was read on 2026-11-07 (T-3473): it names Frances Macbeth Glessner, gives the date 4 March 1892, and suggests she may be in costume for the Benvenuto Cellini dinner party. The museum's site refuses automated access, so the picture itself was not fetched from it; the owner supplied the copy, and that the copy is ICHi-061818 rests on the owner's identification and the record's description. Nothing else in the record says how she stands.
note: Frances Glessner at 44, standing in a glass-roofed conservatory beside a table of potted chrysanthemums, her right hand at her waist, in a long dark gown with large puffed upper sleeves, a fitted bodice and a high ruffled collar; her hair drawn up and back. Her face is a three-quarter view turned to her left, lit from the front, sharp enough to read the eyes, nose, mouth, chin and right ear. The retained catalogue-cited portrait crop is used. Its source face was approximately 90 pixels across; no detail is invented. The full owner-supplied original is not present at the archive path named in the earlier record. Monochrome intensity supplies detail; skin, iris, hair and clothing colours are reconstructed. The photograph does not attest hidden profile depth or exact appearance in another year.
